title: Access Curve Forensics Playbook
author: Amit Desai
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines a reproducible approach for governing elevated access, producing minimal-forensic evidence packages, and performing cross-team evidence handoffs at Redwood Inference. It introduces the ‘Access Curve’ governance model, prescribes a Golden Trace artifact set for access investigations, and documents SDLC and operational controls that ensure evidence is available, tamper-evident, and compliant with retention and legal-hold policies.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-evidence-collection during access incidents by 40% through standardized artifact sets and scripted capture flows.
- Ensure evidence meets audit and legal review expectations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Balance short-lived privilege ergonomics with enforceable review and revocation controls.

Scope:
Applies to: Redwood control plane services, Redwood-managed private control plane components in customer VPCs, and Dedicated control-plane services. Excludes customer-managed application logs unless contractually required.

Key concepts and models:
1) Access Curve model (novel):
   - Concept: Represent every granted entitlement as a curve across two dimensions: breadth (number of distinct resource types / resource IDs the grant touches) and depth (privilege level: read, write, admin, owner).
   - Usage: Automate risk scoring, set default expiry, and require additional approval steps for curves that are both wide and deep.
   - Example enforcement rules (operational):
     * Micro grants: breadth <= 2, depth <= write, default expiry 8h, automated creation via token-service.
     * Escalation windows: breadth <= 5, depth == admin, max 24h, manager approval + ticket link required.
     * Persistent machine grants: only for service principals, must be listed in entitlement registry and reviewed every 90 days.

2) Golden Trace artifact set (forensic minimum):
   - Purpose: Provide a compact, high-confidence timeline that enables root-cause and access-reconstruction without excessively large data exports.
   - Minimal Golden Trace artifacts (required for any access incident):
     * IAM grant record: grantor, grantee, role/permission, scope, timestamp, TTL or expiry.
     * Authentication event: identity token/session id, timestamp, source IP (both public and internal), geo/region tag.
     * Authorization decision log: resource id, action, policy id, evaluated attributes, decision, decision timestamp.
     * Service request trace: request_id, path, canonical args (redacted if PII), response status, latency histogram bucket.
     * Host/container snapshot metadata: container id, pod name, image digest, process list snapshot reference.
   - Optional complements: packet capture excerpt, heap profile for runtime infra, KV cache snapshot when inference cache impacts state.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Security (Policy & Forensics): custodian of Golden Trace definitions, incident evidence lead, keeper of evidence manifest templates.
- Eng-SRE: guarantee log field propagation, sampling policies, and 99th percentile ingestion latency SLOs.
- Eng-Infra: enforce entitlement registry issuance, short-lived credential service, and token rotation.
- Legal & Compliance: make legal-hold decisions, request additional preservation, and sign off on release of evidence to third parties.
- Customer Success: coordinate disclosures to customers under NDA and escalate contractual disclosure requests.

Audit logging minimal schema (required fields):
- timestamp
- request_id
- actor_id
- actor_type (human|service)
- actor_ip
- action
- resource_type
- resource_id
- authz_decision
- policy_id
- session_id
- region
- service_name
- payload_snippet (redacted)

Example compressed log line (illustrative):
{"timestamp":"2026-02-09T18:22:03Z","request_id":"r-2a01f","actor_id":"svc-model-sync","actor_type":"service","actor_ip":"10.8.14.22","action":"model.pull","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"gptx-6b-v2","authz_decision":"allow","policy_id":"pol-entitlement-42","session_id":"s-9c3f","region":"us-west-2","service_name":"model-router","payload_snippet":"{\"seq\":128,...}"}

Retention tiers (policy summary):
- Hot operational traces: 30 days (fast index, used by Eng-SRE for triage).
- Golden Trace artifacts: 24 months in cold archive, with strict RBAC for read and audit logging on access.
- PII-containing artifacts: default 90 days, encrypted-at-rest, accessible only to redacted-audit group unless legal hold applies.
- Legal hold: indefinite until release by Legal; overrides lifecycle.

Retention mapping (text table):
Artifact class | Example artifacts | Default retention | Access group
Short-term traces | request logs, metrics traces | 30d | Eng-SRE, Security (read)
Golden Trace | IAM grant records, authz logs, request traces | 24m | Security (read), Legal (on request)
PII-sensitive | user identifiers in logs | 90d | Security (redacted), Legal
Legal hold | anything on hold | indefinite | Legal, Security

SDLC and deployment controls for RBAC/logging changes:
1. Design note: every PR touching entitlement logic or logging schema must include a short Threat Model update and Golden Trace impact statement.
2. Staging validation: run synthetic identity flows in staging, assert request_id propagation and schema validation (automated).
3. Migration safety: any schema change must be backward compatible for at least 30 days, with migration compatibility matrix documented.
4. Review gates: require at least one Security engineer and one SRE reviewer approval.
5. Post-deploy verification: run a 7-day smoke that samples 1% of requests to ensure Golden Trace completeness; failing smoke triggers automated rollback.

Incident evidence capture and handoff flow (high-level):
1. Initial triage: incident owner creates evidence container incident-<id> and captures available Golden Trace artifacts immediately.
2. Security validation: Forensics team verifies Golden Trace completeness within 2 hours. If incomplete, invoke extended capture.
3. Legal trigger: if PII or contractual data is implicated, Legal is notified within 2 hours; legal hold consideration begins.
4. Customer-facing path: Customer Success only receives redacted artifacts unless the customer has an NDA or specifically consents to full evidence transfer.
5. Evidence packaging: produce an evidence manifest, compute and record checksums (sha256), seal package, and rotate access tokens for the archive.
6. After-action: the postmortem documents any changes to Access Curve thresholds or logging gaps and schedules follow-up actions.

Extended capture flow (when Golden Trace is incomplete):
- Host/container snapshot (Eng-SRE):
  * kubectl exec -n <namespace> <pod> -- tar -czf /tmp/diag-<id>.tgz /var/log /proc/*/cmdline
  * aws s3 cp /tmp/diag-<id>.tgz s3://forensic-temp/incident-<id>/ --acl private
- Preserve system time sources: capture NTP/chrony state and hardware clock output; include time-sync metadata in manifest.
- If packet-level evidence is necessary, capture limited pcap slices around the incident window and upload to secure archive.

Access reviews, automation, and exception handling:
- Quarterly entitlement audit: automated job produces Access Curve heatmaps per team and flags top 5% widest and deepest curves for manual review.
- Automated expiry enforcement: token-service issues short-lived credentials by default; manual extensions must attach a ticket and manager approval.
- Exception registry: any deviation from policy is recorded in the exception register with justification, owner, and expiry date; exceptions are surfaced in quarterly reviews.

SLOs and monitoring for evidence pipelines:
- Auth log ingestion latency (99th): < 90s.
- Golden Trace completeness: >= 99.5% per 24h window; gaps >0.5% trigger a Sev-2 investigation.
- Forensic archive availability: 99.95% monthly.

Appendix A  Evidence manifest template (text):
- incident_id: <string>
- collected_by: <uid>
- collection_start: <ISO8601>
- artifacts: comma-separated filenames
- checksums: sha256sum file attached
- chain_of_custody: chronological entries (timestamp | actor | action)

FAQ (short):
Q: Developer needs elevated access for a weekend debug. What is the recommended path?
A: Use the escalation grant workflow. Create a single 24h admin grant scoped narrowly, attach an internal ticket, get manager sign-off. For longer debug windows, renew the 24h grant with a short post-period justification and an entry in the exception register.

Q: How do I escalate if Golden Trace artifacts are missing from logs?
A: Raise a security incident, initiate the extended capture flow, and contact Eng-SRE to snapshot containers and system logs. If PII is involved, notify Legal immediately.
